_comment: Sites where a synchronous std::process::Command is waited on with no
time bound, and that are ACCEPTED. Enforced by
scripts/check_untimed_subprocess.py and
.github/workflows/forbid-untimed-subprocess.yml.
'format' is the schema version. The checker REJECTS any other value
rather than matching nothing against it, because 'matches nothing'
reads as 'the site was fixed' and would ungate every entry at once.
'site' is '<repo-relative path>::<qualified fn>' — qualified by every
enclosing impl / trait / mod / outer fn, so `impl A { fn run }` and
`impl B { fn run }` are different sites, as are `impl Bar<u8>` and
`impl Bar<u16>`. A trait impl reads as '<Type as Trait>'. The key is
stable across edits above and below the call, which a line number is
not.
'waits' names WHAT this function currently waits on, one normalized
program per untimed wait: a string-literal program as its lowercased
basename without '.exe', a computed one as 'dyn:<last identifier>', a
Command handed in by a caller or built by a helper as '?' /
'fn:<helper>'. The checker fails if the real list differs in ANY way —
longer, shorter, or the same length with a different program — so the
baseline can only shrink and cannot silently rot.
A COUNT alone could not see a SWAP. Replacing a baselined `osascript`
one-shot with `Command::new("aws").args(["s3","ls",…]).output()`
keeps the count at 1, so a count ratchet stays green while an unbounded
NETWORK call ships under prose written for a local one-shot. The
program token is what makes the swap visible; it is deliberately NOT a
hash of the call text, which would go red on `git status` ->
`git status --porcelain` — an edit that cannot invalidate any reason.
'reason' is REQUIRED and must say why an unbounded wait is acceptable
HERE — i.e. why this code is not on a periodic or hot path.
'reason_covers_waits' is the list that reason was written against and
MUST equal 'waits'. --update-baseline clears the reason whenever a
wait is ADDED or SWAPPED (never for a pure removal), so neither a new
wait nor a different program can inherit prose written for another
call; and editing 'waits' by hand without touching the reason fails on
the mismatch.
Do NOT add an entry to silence a periodic caller. Route it through
run_probe / output_with_timeout / run_with_timeout instead.

exemptions.reason: One-shot macOS `security find-generic-password` attribute query on the OAuth-refresh decision path, not a timer. It is a local Keychain read with no -w/-g, so it never prompts and never waits on a network or a lock.

Teardown path: `taskkill /F /T` against a pid we are already killing. It runs once per pi child at end-of-session, and blocking here is bounded by the OS's own terminate call rather than by the dead child.

This IS the 'run an AI CLI session to completion' primitive — a claude/pi run legitimately takes minutes to hours, so any wall-clock bound here would be wrong. Its lifetime is governed by the session's own cancellation, and it is one call per user-started session, never periodic. BOTH waits are that same primitive, one per arm of a single `match`: with a DoctorHandle the child is spawned with piped stdio and reaped by `child.wait_with_output()` so the run can be registered with Doctor first; without one it is the plain `cmd.output()`. Neither arm can run twice, and the second was invisible to this gate until the receiver resolver learned to read a `Command` arriving as a function PARAMETER — which is also why both tokens are '?': the caller chose the program.
Standalone CLI binary (`qontinui_cli`), not the runner: one `git` plumbing read. It has no tokio runtime and therefore no blocking pool to exhaust; the process is one command and exits.

The PATH shim's whole job is to become the real tool: it must inherit stdio and wait for exactly as long as the real `git`/`cargo` takes. A timeout here would truncate the very command the caller asked for. Separate binary, no tokio runtime.

Runs a user-authored check command (lint/typecheck/test) through `cmd /C`, with a runtime that is legitimately unbounded. The budget belongs to the check step's own configured timeout, not to a blanket wrapper here. Invoked per user-started check run, never on a timer.
Tauri command — fires on a user opening the instances view. `git worktree list --porcelain` is a local plumbing read against an already-open repo.
One-shot macOS Keychain attribute query (`security find-generic-password`) inside `coord doctor`, an operator-invoked diagnostic. Attribute-only (no -w/-g), so it never prompts.
Tauri command: the operator clicked 'force stop' on a specific pid. `taskkill /F /T` on a named pid, once per click.

This IS a bounded wrapper — the shutdown path's counterpart to process_helpers::run_with_timeout, and the seam every drain/taskkill caller was routed through. Its `.wait_with_output()` runs only on the branch where `try_wait()` has ALREADY reported the child exited, so it drains pipes on a dead child and cannot block on the child's lifetime; the deadline branch kills and reaps instead. Baselined rather than whole-file skipped because a file-level skip is what let a fourth non-wrapper hide beside the real ones in process_helpers.rs — a new raw wait added to drain.rs still surfaces as a separate site with an empty reason.

User-requested stop of a task run, once per tracked AI pid on the stop path only: `taskkill /F /T /PID` on Windows and `kill -9` on the `#[cfg(not(windows))]` arm. Both are one-shot terminations of a named pid, bounded by the OS's own terminate call.
User/agent-requested stop of an AI analysis: `taskkill /F /T` once per tracked pid, on the stop path only.
`cargo --version` behind a `Lazy` — it runs at most ONCE per process lifetime and the result is cached forever. Not a periodic caller by construction.
`mypy --version` / `python -m mypy --version` behind a `Lazy` — at most once per process, cached forever.
`tsc --version` resolution for a typecheck scope. Runs on the operator/agent-initiated typecheck path, not a timer, and only after `find_tsc` has already located the binary on disk.
Failure path only: the headless browser did not connect within its own timeout, so we `taskkill` the pid we just spawned. Reached once per failed spawn, on an agent-initiated request.
User/agent-requested stop of a task run: `taskkill /F /T` once per tracked AI pid, on the stop path only.
One ffmpeg frame-extraction pass per verification request, bounded by `-frames:v`. Agent-initiated, never on a timer; a transcode of a long trace legitimately takes minutes.

Runs the workspace's own build — `npm run build` via `cmd /C` on Windows and `sh -c` elsewhere, plus `cargo check` when a Cargo.toml is present. Unbounded by nature, and the point of the check is to let it finish. One pass per agent-initiated verification request.

Executes a user-authored orchestrator hook command through `cmd /C`. Its runtime is whatever the operator's script does; a blanket budget here would silently truncate hooks. Fires per task-run lifecycle event, not on a timer.

Executes a user-authored verification command (build/test/lint) through whichever shell the platform resolves to — a discovered `bash_path`, `cmd /C`, or `sh -c` — with a runtime that is legitimately unbounded. Budget belongs to the verification step's own config. One pass per orchestrator iteration, driven by task progress rather than a clock.

Runs a Playwright test script via `npx` (twice: the Windows and non-Windows arms). A browser test legitimately runs for minutes and already carries its own `timeout_ms`. User/agent-initiated per run, never periodic.
Same as `run_script`, for the inline-script form: two `npx` invocations across the platform arms, the Playwright run owns its own timeout, and it is user/agent-initiated per run.

`profile_cli` is a standalone operator CLI for editing the user PATH; this reads it with one `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command`. No tokio runtime, no blocking pool; the process runs one command and exits.
Same as `read_path_scope`: one `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive` invocation from a standalone operator CLI, no tokio runtime, one command per process.
`where.exe git` fallback, reached only when none of the well-known bash.exe paths exist. `where.exe` is a local PATH scan; the call happens while preparing a user-authored shell step, not on a timer.

Checks whether a chrome process exists while assembling a diagnostics report after a failed test: `tasklist` filtered to chrome.exe on Windows, `pgrep -x chrome` on unix with a `ps aux` fallback when pgrep is absent. Operator/agent-initiated, one pass per report.
Runs `npx playwright test` — directly on unix, and through `cmd /c` on Windows. The run carries its own `timeout_ms` and legitimately takes minutes. One invocation per user/agent-started test run.
Runs a user-authored python test script whose runtime is unbounded by design. One invocation per user/agent-started test run.

Runs the repo's own configured test command through `cmd /c` on Windows or `sh -c` elsewhere — unbounded by nature, and the budget belongs to the test config. One invocation per user/agent-started run.
User-triggered window activation (`wmctrl`/`xdotool`), one pass per click. Local X11 clients that return in milliseconds or fail immediately when no display is present.
User-triggered window activation via `osascript`, one pass per click.
User-triggered window enumeration (`wmctrl -l -p`, `xdotool search`), one pass per click on the window picker.
User-triggered window enumeration via `osascript`, one pass per click on the window picker.
Per-window `xdotool getwindowpid` / `getwindowname` follow-ups inside the user-triggered enumeration above; same one-pass-per-click lifetime.
`node --version` with stdio nulled — a fail-fast startup precondition check for the wrapper install pipeline, run once before installs rather than on a schedule.
